blocks.text: Corporate data can be leaked in different ways (i.e., through web mail, cloud storage, social media, and a variety of other applications). You can use the Zscaler Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy to protect your organization from data loss.

If your organization has a third-party DLP solution, Zscaler can forward information about transactions that trigger DLP policies to your third-party solution. Zscaler uses secure Internet Content Adaptation Protocol (ICAP) to do this. However, the Zscaler service does not take ICAP responses from your DLP solution. Zscaler only monitors or blocks content according to the policy you configure, then forwards information about transactions so that your organization can take any necessary remediation steps.
DLP provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Use the Zscaler DLP policy to monitor and prevent the leakage of sensitive data.
Use Zscaler custom and predefined DLP engines to detect and take action on sensitive data.
Forward information about transactions that trigger DLP policies to your third-party DLP solution.

blocks.text: The following are the different types of DLP policy rules you can configure. Your policy can use one or more of these options simultaneously.

blocks.item: Monitor or block data using Zscaler DLP engines
With this option, Zscaler:
Scans content with Zscaler DLP engines for specific data.
Allows or blocks the transaction.
(Optional) Sends your auditor a notification.
The following is an illustration of the process that occurs when you block data using Zscaler DLP engines. To learn more, see Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Content Inspection.
Monitor or block data using Zscaler DLP engines, then forward information to a third-party DLP solution
With this option, Zscaler:
Scans content with Zscaler DLP engines for specific data.
Allows or blocks the transaction.
(Optional) Sends your auditor a notification.
Sends the following information about the violation to your third-party DLP solution via secure ICAP:
Client IP and username of users attempting to send data (via ICAP X-headers).
A copy of the HTTP POST request that contains the relevant file or content (if content is from HTTP Form data or a text file). The host URL that the user was sending content to is also included here.

The following is an illustration of the process that occurs when you block data using Zscaler DLP engines and forward information to your third-party DLP solution. To learn more, see Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Content Inspection.
Monitor or block data based on specific criteria, then forward information to a third-party DLP solution
With this option, Zscaler does not use its DLP engines. Instead, the service does the following:
Detects content that meets the criteria you select (for example, destination URL category or file type).
Allows or blocks the content.
(Optional) Sends your auditor a notification.
Sends the following information about the violation to your third-party DLP solution via secure ICAP:
Client IP and username of users attempting to send data (via ICAP X-headers).
A copy of the HTTP POST request that contains the relevant file or content (if content is from HTTP Form data or a text file). The host URL that the user was sending content to is also included here.
The following is an illustration of the process that takes place when you configure DLP policies for this option. To learn more, see Configuring DLP Policy Rules without Content Inspection.
Monitor or block data based on data size to leverage Zscaler's DLP policy without scanning for specific data within the content.

blocks.text: To see how this policy fits into the overall order of policy enforcement, see Understanding Policy Enforcement. To learn more about Endpoint DLP, see About Endpoint Data Loss Prevention.

blocks.heading: About the Data Loss Prevention Page

blocks.text: The appearance of the Data Loss Prevention page varies slightly, depending on whether Evaluate All Rules mode is enabled in your organization. To learn more, see Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Evaluate All Rules Mode Enabled.
On the Data Loss Prevention page (Data Security > Inline DLP > Data Loss Prevention), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Add and configure a DLP policy rule.
Select Rule Label to view the rules based on the rule labels. The rules are grouped under the associated rule labels. See image.
You can expand or collapse all the rule labels using the Expand All or Collapse All buttons.
Search for a DLP policy rule.
Modify the table and its columns.

View a list of all configured DLP policy rules and exception rules that were configured for your organization. Exception rules are child rules that allow you to exclude specific users or groups in your organization that need to perform tasks as part of a necessary workflow that might otherwise violate inline DLP policy. For policy rules and exception rules, you can see:
Rule Order: The policy rule's order number. You can sort this column.

Rule order is not enforced for parent rules when the Zscaler service is configured to evaluate all rules. Exception rule evaluation stops at the first match, and an exception replaces a parent rule upon match. To learn more, see Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Evaluate All Rules Mode Enabled.

Admin Rank: Click Edit and select an admin rank 0 to 7 (0 is the highest rank) from the drop-down menu. This option appears if you enable Admin Ranking on the Advanced Settings page. Your assigned admin rank determines the values you can select (e.g., you cannot select a rank higher than your own). The rule's admin rank determines the value you can select for rule order, so that a rule with a higher admin rank always precedes a rule with a lower admin rank. You can sort this column.
Rule Name: The name of the rule. You can sort this column.
DLP Engines: The DLP engines used to evaluate the rule.
Cloud Application: The cloud applications covered by the rule.
Cloud Application Instances: The cloud application instances allow you to create instances for cloud applications where you can add specific instance identifiers (e.g., domains).
Users: The users to whom the rule applies.
Groups: The user groups to which the rule applies.
Locations: The locations covered by the rule. To apply this rule to unauthenticated traffic, the rule must apply to all locations.
Location Groups: The location groups covered by the rule.
Departments: The departments to which the rule applies.
Domain Profiles: The domain profiles covered by the rule.
File Types: The types of files evaluated by the rule. Note that the file types supported by Zscaler DLP Engine rules differ from those supported by External DLP Engine rules.
Protocols: The protocols to which the rule applies.
Source IP Groups: The source IP groups covered by the rule.
Time: The time intervals during which the rule applies.
URL Categories: The URL categories covered by the rule.
User Risk Profile: The user risk profiles used during the policy evaluation.
Workload Groups: The workload groups covered by the rule.
ZPA Application Segment: The Private Access application segments covered by the rule. The list displays only those Private Access application segments that have the Source IP Anchor option enabled.
Content Locations: The sections of a file or transaction that are evaluated by the rule.
Rule Action: The Rule Action section provides options such as Allow or Block the action. For example, Block might be selected to prevent certain activities.
Label: The label and description of the rule, if available.
Description: The description of the rule, if available.
Actions: Displays whether the rule is Enabled or Disabled.
Parent rules and exception rules apply only when Evaluate All Rules mode is enabled. To learn more, see Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Evaluate All Rules Mode Enabled.
Edit the rule.
Duplicate or delete the rule.
Add an exception rule to a parent rule (Evaluate All Rules Mode only).
